articles.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
articles.summary: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.
body: Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats.

articles.title: Netflix CEO admits app may bury stuff you want to watch under stuff you don’t
articles.summary: The streaming wars, or the battle to be the top streaming company, are ongoing, according to Ted Sarandos, a co-CEO of what many would consider today’s frontrunner. When it comes to subscribers, no streaming service has more than Netflix, which reported having over 325 million subscribers as of…
body: But in an interview with Bloomberg published today, Sarandos noted that people are still spending significant time watching traditional broadcast TV.

“The streaming wars are continuing as we go. Half of television engagement in the United States is still linear, old television,” he said, without specifying the source of the statistic. According to analysis from Nielsen, streaming represented 49.6 percent of TV viewing in August, with 36.4 percent coming from broadcast and cable. That still suggests a sizable amount of viewing time for streaming providers to target.
As Netflix seeks to strengthen its lead against rivals like YouTube and Skydance, there’s extra pressure for it to deliver hit shows and movies.

I think as Netflix has grown and matured and the business has grown and matured around us, that hit rate really matters. And you’ve got to get ahead of ‘are we on a path to continue [and] maintain that hit rate in the US particularly, but everywhere in the world?’ And I’d say the business is working everywhere in the world, including the US, but we should be doing better in the US than we were. And we’ve got to really focus on our ability to do that.

articles.title: PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI
articles.summary: Disruption comes at critical moment, with Grand Theft Auto VI one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in history. PlayStation has suffered widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in recent gaming history.
body: The disruption emerged Wednesday, causing frustrated players to flood social media with complaints about failed logins and server connection problems downloading games and updates.
PlayStation’s official network status page acknowledged problems affecting its gaming and social services, which has left players struggling to access online features.
“You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We’re working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience,” the alert read.

Many affected users said their internet connections were working normally, suggesting the problems were specifically affecting PlayStation’s online services. Some PS5 owners said that their consoles successfully completed internet connection tests, only for the “Sign in to online services” check to fail.

articles.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
articles.summary: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core.
body: The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.

This isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses “hybrid post-quantum key exchange” based on the quantum-safe ML-KEM; and remote desktop authentication and PowerShell script block logging get stricter as well.

Microsoft’s native NVMe storage stack was originally introduced via an update to Windows Server 2025, but it required administrators to enable it manually. The update eliminated NVMe translation through a SCSI stack while improving speeds and reducing overhead. The redesigned stack will now be default-on in Windows Server 2028.

articles.title: Nvidia’s rise, visualized
articles.summary: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That's how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change.
body: It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals, and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so?

But I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake.

It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you. I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now.

If you’re on a desktop OS, you could mouse over each dot in our chart above to see the staggering sums. But we built another way to visualize the rise of Nvidia I like even better. It’s a horizontal bar graph that not only puts Nvidia’s revenue growth in perspective, but shows you its monster profits right alongside them — plus the world events that made Nvidia a star.
points: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do?
That's how much pure profit Nvidia now makes.

articles.title: Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights. Though, it turns out that you can already get a great deal on the 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II, one of our favorite OLED televisions.
body: My colleague John Higgins praised the Bravia 8 II for its excellent image quality and engaging picture, though those positive traits are consistent with almost all OLED TVs. What sets this one apart is its impressive image processing, the bold colors from its quantum dot-equipped OLED panel, and that it looks great right out of the box (although he recommends using Professional mode). The screen was awarded the top spot at 2025’s Value Electronics TV Shootout, beating out similar offerings from competitors like Panasonic, LG, and Samsung.

For gaming, the panel can reach up to 120Hz at 4K, with both variable refresh rate and automatic low-latency mode to ensure that your content looks and feels good to play. The connectivity includes two HDMI 2.1 (one with eARC), and two HDMI 2.0 ports, giving you plenty of inputs for consoles and a Blu-ray player, among other gadgets. We spotted some color fringing of certain colors in dark scenes, and lamented the lack of a but it’s an otherwise excellent screen we can easily recommend.

articles.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
articles.summary: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.
body: When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.
“Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for….”

In at least one case, Muse told a staffer surprised by a similarly out-of-context offer to message a seller about a coffee table that it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”

Raising the most concern were random outputs that appeared to share private user data. For example, a perplexed Meta staffer chatting with Muse about fishing got a random extra response, seemingly sharing balances from two unknown bank accounts. That output said, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”

articles.title: Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
articles.summary: Instagram's latest update will allow you to edit your Stories without losing your views, likes, or replies. You can now edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing your Story, Instagram head Adam Mosseri has announced.
body: You can edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings in your Stories for up to 15 minutes after sharing.

Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted Instagram working on this feature in April, but now it’s official. Previously, you had to delete and repost your Story to fix a typo or add a song that you forgot to include.
You can edit your post by opening your Story and selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner. From there, tap “Edit Story” to start making changes.

In addition to editable Stories, Instagram announced that it’s launching new fonts, colors, and shapes for stickers, as well as presenting them on sticker sheets that are supposed to be easier to browse. The platform is also making changes to the way you select multiple photos and adding new blur, colors, and gradient background options.

articles.title: US senators urge White House AI chief to fix vulnerabilities after mass outages
articles.summary: As Democrats flag AI bank breaches and cyber-attacks in Japan, Jay Clayton says system failures happen. US politics live – latest updates. A bipartisan pair of US senators are calling on Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence and AI czar, to identify and fix vulnerabilities in the US’s…
body: Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate commerce, science, and transportation committee, and Mike Rounds, the Republican chair of the Senate subcommittee on cybersecurity, sent a letter to Clayton on Tuesday, outlining concerns sparked by reports of AI accessing major banks, cyber-attacks in Japan and more.

“The fundamental problem is that AI can discover software weaknesses and help attackers exploit them faster than many organizations can respond,” Cantwell and Rounds wrote to Clayton, who is also serving as the White House AI czar.
“Even when fixes are available, testing and installing patches across interconnected systems can take weeks or months, potentially disrupting essential services,” the senators wrote.

Over the last week, tech outages at major banks, workplace communication systems and even federal infrastructure like the Federal Aviation Administration – triggering a four-hour nationwide flight stoppage that grounded or delayed thousands of flights – have raised alarms about potential cyber-attacks.

articles.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
articles.summary: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.
body: This week, the Trump administration made it significantly harder for Chinese companies to access some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. For years, tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance could rent computing power from data centers overseas, allowing them to use powerful Nvidia chips they were generally prohibited from physically importing into China. This is known as remote access.

But under new plans announced on Monday, overseas data centers that want to provide large amounts of computing power to China will have to get special licenses and deal with other annoying new kinds of red tape. The White House also imposed stricter rules on shipments of advanced chips to five countries, including Singapore and Malaysia, where US officials suspect significant levels of smuggling may have taken place.

These are not new policy ideas, and similar proposals have been kicking around in Washington for a while. But the timing of Monday’s announcement is impossible to ignore. Yes, this is about Jensen Huang’s sex life.

articles.title: Players say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto V with one last drive
articles.summary: For more than a decade, GTA Online and its virtual California has hosted the criminal capers of millions of players. As many of them prepare to move on to GTA VI, they are marking the end of an era. Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?
body: The virtual streets of Grand Theft Auto Online’s Los Santos will be spared from their usual explosions and high-speed car chases tonight, as hundreds of players meet for a final journey across the video game’s world before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI at midnight.

Rockstar Games’ multiplayer criminal sandbox normally prompts hostility between its millions of players by giving them ample access to guns, bombs and fighter jets. But fans took it upon themselves to peacefully cruise across the game world together for “one last drive” in virtual California, before the next chapter in the series arrives.

Willy, who goes by zarki_34 online, has played GTA Online for thousands of hours over the last decade. He has organised several of his own final drive events. “[GTA Online] has been part of my life for 13 years … I’m now 26,” he says. “I’ve spent half my life with this game.”
His route took players from the centre of the game’s Los Angeles-inspired city, across rugged coastlines and through so-Cal countryside in one singular trip.

articles.title: An AI Debt Collection Service Exposed 6.6 Million Accounts and 315,000 Call Recordings
articles.summary: A pair of serious vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana platform would have allowed attackers to access troves of detailed sensitive information, including emails, texts, and credit reports.
body: Two vulnerabilities in the India-based AI-driven debt collection platform CreditNirvana exposed 6.6 million accounts and about 315,000 call recordings from the company's agentic call center, according to research released on Wednesday. Owned by the Indian fintech company Perfios, the platform is built to “read a borrower’s full context, decide the next best action, and execute it autonomously, continuously, and within policy.”

The bugs were patched in CreditNirvana's systems in June and were disclosed publicly in October. But independent researcher Eaton Zveare, who found and disclosed them, notes that, while the vulnerabilities were active, they exposed personal information on millions of borrowers. Details about financial collections are inherently—perhaps obviously—sensitive, because they relate to unpaid accounts or debts and often involve extensive documentation of people's personal histories.
points: A pair of serious vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana platform would have allowed attackers to access troves of detailed sensitive information, including emails, texts, and credit reports.
